column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3d background, the field's first map of income risk by source (gifts high, government low, earned moderate); Laura's ten fixed $50,000 payments are the column the map lacks; 1990s US case studies, mostly human services, so store and one clause at most.

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d, directors' own words on stable operating money; quoted second-hand (Froelich quoting Gronbjerg 1993), so cite as Froelich; drop money in the bank in the literal sense for Laura, whose money is Treasuries held for her at one broker, not a bank deposit.

Thu 19 Nov: store, foundation money is episodic and multiyear grants buffer it; near Q55-018 and Q9-010 (capital is episodic), adds Froelich's wording only; 1990s US foundations, and Taiwan firms renew a year at a time (Q50-020).

Thu 19 Nov: store, the founding volatility study (gift-reliant groups swing more); abstract and two secondary accounts only, coefficients unread, so S 3; background for row 6, never a figure in the report.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d or 2.3 store, Bridgespan's Foster: 90% of nonprofits reaching $50m take 90% from one source, so one large reliable source is normal, not a weakness; read in SSIR, Foster's study not read; very large US groups and growth, not survival.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d store, donative arts groups' revenue swings about 40% more (M. Kim 2014, working paper tables read); fix the use column: it is the whole revenue that swings about 40% more, not its gifts; a free residency being donative is Keel inference from Q135-041.

Thu 19 Nov: store, investment income is the volatile source in nonprofit data; abstract only (S 3), no figures; supports why the payments sit in Treasuries held to their dates rather than in a market-valued pot.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d and 3e (or 2.3's diversify Laura aha), the field's standard defence, many income sources, stopped protecting US nonprofits in 2008-09; corrects H7-080's lean on diversifying the residency; say US, one recession, and can fall in the same downturn, never fall together.

Thu 19 Nov: store behind claim 2, in 2007-09 US government grants steadied revenue and investment income swung most; quote the journal's figures, never the dissertation's, and in words only; drop Laura's investment income is fixed at each date, since an iBond fund's payout is never called fixed (say owned, counted after fees and the 0.5% margin).

Thu 19 Nov: evidence for the register's can fall in the same downturn (IPS l.9, CANON B4); Choi's summary of unread studies, so S 3; US 2008 only, and its list names government funding, which in Taiwan rose (CANON B4, Q10d-020), so never quote it of Taiwan's co-sponsors and never simultaneously or fall together in report words.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d or 3e store, US arts revenue moves with GDP (0.51) while all nonprofit revenue does not (-0.04); open access, figures read; GDP is not share prices (Taiwan 2020: TAIEX up, Q50-029), so never a figure in 3d and never a correlation for the payments beyond a fixed sum cannot co-move.

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3a, the field now ties reserve size to how gift-reliant income is, and donors dislike large liquid assets (pairs with Q135-016, Q22-038); the reserve advice is the authors' untested suggestion.

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3a, nonprofit revenue moves more than one-for-one with local income while spending moves half as much; fix the use column: Q135-040 says some residencies' applications more than doubled, not that applications doubled; all US nonprofits, local downturns.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d store with row 11, revenue swings predict closure (10% more volatility, 7-14% more dissolution risk); abstract only (S 3), whole-budget volatility, US 2010-18; fills Q140's missing step, never a multiplier for Laura's payments.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a store, in the 2020 shutdown groups with reserves cut hours and staff less, and arts groups were hit harder; abstract only (S 3); a group's own reserve, not a founder's dated payments, so a clause of support at most.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, what owned running money lets the residency do, in a grantee's words (plan 66%, staff 26%; hiring is hard with only 12 months guaranteed); CEP PDF read at source; Q55-018 holds the rarity, this the benefit; a US grantee's words, never Laura's.
Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d, core money lets a group win restricted project money and hire on longer contracts, so leverage rather than substitution; one Mexico City example in a blog post.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d store, a foundation stepped back from multiyear grants in 2008-09 when long commitments felt riskier; one US anecdote, so pair with Q50-008 (NCAF's five-year pledges that faded) as Taiwan's own case; say other funders' promises can be withdrawn, Laura's are owned.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e honest limit, owned running money can tempt a charity to fundraise less; re-read at source by the rater: crowding out about 75%, due primarily to reduced fundraising, $10,000 cuts fundraising by $1,410 and donations by $7,570, match a fraction; government grants, not a founder; fix a secure $50,000 to owned (never secured, Q147).

Thu 19 Nov: store, crowd-out is mostly a lab result; abstract only (S 3); fix the use column: field data give +$0.06 per dollar, near zero, so say little effect in real data, never that support and gifts move together.

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d, government grants crowd in gifts by signalling quality; abstract only (S 3), published 2014 version unread, young-organisation result unchecked; a founder's signal is already carried by the lead-gift rows (Q11a-002, H3-093).
Thu 19 Nov: store, arts-specific crowd-in in US performing arts 1998-2003 (+$0.14 to +$1.15 per dollar), dance a small crowd-out; abstract only (S 3).

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d with Q22-038, donors give less to small arts groups told of government money; a survey experiment on hypothetical gifts, publisher excerpt and Wallace review only (S 3); shares are Americans for the Arts 2012 figures.

Thu 19 Nov: store behind claim 3, the larger meta-analysis finds a small positive link between diversification and financial health, weaker in the US; abstract only (S 3); the report should not lean on diversify the residency.
Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 or 3d store with row 24, diversification had little effect on vulnerability; abstract only (S 3); kills a residency needs many sources to be safe, which tempers H7-080.

Thu 19 Nov: store behind claim 3, concentration is low risk when the main source is steady (government grants, earned income); abstract only (S 3); pair with Q9-015, where UK grant dependence was the danger: the risk is a source that can be withdrawn, which Laura's owned payments are not.
Thu 19 Nov: store, the field's ideal is a source that does not fall with the others; abstract only (S 3); note it finds diversification can reduce downside risk in 2008-12 data, a balance to row 8.

Thu 19 Nov: store for the problem class only; Kingma (1993) not read, known through Froelich and Myser, so S 2; cite as Froelich's account and never quote Kingma's words (stability against predictability) as his.
Thu 19 Nov: store, arts nonprofits' four sources read as a portfolio with an efficient frontier, and a count of sources (HHI) is not the test; abstract only (S 3), no frontier figures.

Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q9-015 (via Q140-013): concentration itself is not the danger; Greenlee and Trussel known only second-hand, and Keating et al. and Myser define distress differently, so S 2; Q9-015 holds the read-at-source version.

Thu 19 Nov: store colour for claim 3 only (the absolute rules line); never a voice model for 3d, since the report's voice comes from Caplet's own writing (Book 17), and a savings account is not the IPS's choice for the payments (Treasuries held to their dates).

Thu 19 Nov: twin of H9-114 and Q16-038 (NORI's 25 percent or 3 months, re-read at source by the rater); its new parts ride on Q16-038: no one size fits all, 5 to 6 years of modest surpluses, 1,516 of 3,154 DC nonprofits below the minimum and 520 (17%) negative; guard kept: three to six months is Propel's, never NORI's (the white paper never says it).

Thu 19 Nov: 3a aha candidate beside Q16-038, re-read at source by the rater (p.9: a Plan B naming held assets, organizations and individuals, for a group new and trying to reach a sustainable size); NORI's Plan B is an emergency fallback, so never Laura's plan is that Plan B or the IPS is that Plan B: say the funders' own standard lets a new group name an individual's held assets instead of a reserve, and Laura's payments go further, the running money itself, owned and dated; to a cold aha test.

Thu 19 Nov: store behind claim 2; SMU's unrestricted contributed revenue rose 3% real in its sample of arts groups' 2020 fiscal years, while Giving USA counted arts giving down 7.5% in 2020 (Q12b-021, CANON B4), so name the measure and never say US arts gifts rose in 2020 bare; relief money was one-off.
Thu 19 Nov: store only, a 2020 projection of a deficit of 26% of expenses; measured gifts did not fall as forecast (row 34), so never as what happened.

Thu 19 Nov: store; the Great Recession fall is 5.0% here and 3.5% in Q1b-023 (BEA vintages move, Q1c-009), and the 3.4% GDP fall for 2020 is also a vintage, so cite one dated release and never both; never for her career line (Census -7.8%).

Thu 19 Nov: store, adds FY2021 (-17.9%) to Q4b-022's US state arts series: US public arts money is cut in both kinds of shock, and late; US states only, never said of Taiwan (CANON B4, rows 41 and 44).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d store, arts groups were hit hardest in 2008-09 and funders rarely pay for reserves; a review of others' work (S 3), cite as the Wallace Foundation review; drop cushion for Laura's money (WORDS), say her owned operating money.

Thu 19 Nov: twin of H3-112 (Baumol's cost disease) and Q102-025; the 19.2% is Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 8d's $43,368 and $35,032 (checked), and 8d already says the 2042 payment buys about 70% of today's $50,000.

Thu 19 Nov: store for 3d, Taiwan's performing groups in 2005 took about half from earned income, 40% from government and about 8% from foundations, firms and individuals (Keel sums on NCAF's 2009 study, Q135-035's source); 2005 performing arts only; Laura's co-sponsors fund the building, not running costs.
Thu 19 Nov: CANON B4 guard, Taiwan doubled its flagship troupe grant to NT$232.45m in 2009, the highest ever, beside Q10d-020's +29.1%; a political pledge, never a counter-cyclical rule.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d Taiwanese evidence, public troupes whose budgets were set the year before were relatively free from the pandemic's effects; a conference paper (S 4) about state bodies a legislature can still cut (Q10d); fix Laura's payments are bought in January 2027 to most of each owned from January 2027, all ten from January 2028 (NUMBERS 1); check the author's own romanisation (the file says Dr. Chi).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or 3d, Taiwan's 2020 ticket sales fell about a third while the TAIEX rose 22.8% (Q50-029): the shock that hits arts money need not be a fall in shares, which is why the register says can; one ticketing system, and a free residency earns little from tickets.

Thu 19 Nov: CANON B4 guard with row 41, Taiwan's National Performing Arts Center in 2020: own income -44.3%, government money +7.8% (Keel arithmetic checked: 75.50% to 85.65% government share); so 3d's can fall points at companies and earned income, never Taiwan's government.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e limit said plainly, the plan owns ten years of running money, not the residency's future, and co-sponsors hear what ends in 2042; Keel synthesis of read rows (S 3); cite Capital is episodic; revenue is forever to NFF (Q9-010, which carries Q11b-024).
